S. flava var. atropurpurea 'super dark' Okaloosa Co, FL starting off...kinda red! Sorry, not re-naming this to S. flava var. atropurpurea 'kinda red' Okaloosa Co, FL, haha! The traps started off like this last year just like this, and for those of you who are growing atropurpureas from Okaloosa Co, FL, when you see them red even before the traps fully open, you know they can color up a lot more as the traps age. As an aside, even if they start off greenish, some of these clones (ie. the giant ones here: sarracenia.proboards.com/thread/4511/flava-var-atropurpurea-giant-okaloosa ) will still turn solid red after the traps age.

Pics taken 4/20/20:




I know some of you are tempted to call this a rubricorpora, but to that I say look at the picture in the previous post:

posts.body_html:
This clone hasn't quite colored up yet, but the everything is way behind this year, so it's not so surprising. It's also been a bit cloudy and we haven't had as much sun as we normally do. This super dark clone only really colors up as the traps age quite a bit. Interestingly our weeks of cold weather has slowed down both pitcher growth and pitcher aging! For what it's worth, I guess each individual pitcher has a longer "shelf life" when grown under cooler conditions.

Pics taken 5/11/20:


The shape of the traps are consistent: last year, the plant looked almost exactly the same!




We'll see what happens in 1-2 weeks. this morning, it did look like the traps are starting to get slightly darker, but I'll wait until they're 2AT super dark...okaloosa Co, FL! Man, that was a bad joke, but if you chuckled, props home skillet!
